unmutated.G1:published-is-current: No matrix entry breaks it, and a realistic mistake could: it asserts that after a Published outcome current() is exactly that generation, and an implementation that returns Published but swaps the live generation in late, stale, or only the first time is not in the matrix. The first-publication half is also asserted by P1:consistent-published (current().isPresent()), and a stale current would repeat numbers, which G4:consecutive would show; but the later-publication case is pinned only here. Allowed for now; a mutant that stores only the first generation would earn it.
unmutated.G2:broken-optional-left-out: The same rule as G2:optional-dropped-transitively (ShallowDropGenerations) reached through the other way an entry breaks: an optional entry that an ERROR finding names (no part is made for it) and the binding that names it both leave, and both are named. DanglingTolerantGenerations fails it (the binding is published pointing at the entry with no part), but only because it resolves nothing. An implementation that treats OPTIONAL like REQUIRED and refuses on any broken entry passes the matrix; that policy half is also asserted by G7:optional-rejection-left-out and the seeded laws G2:seeded-refusal and G2:seeded-survivors, none of which has a dedicated entry.
unmutated.G2:dropped-reported: Restates G7:accounted for the entries an optional drop removes: offer() holds every publication to 'in the manifest or named by a finding', which is the same check on the same entries, and TrustingGenerations is the entry that fails that ground. DanglingTolerantGenerations, ShallowDropGenerations and FirstFindingGenerations fail this label too, but only because they do not resolve, resolve shallowly or report too little. A dropper that removes the right entries and writes no reference:dangling finding for them is not in the matrix, and would be caught here and by G7:accounted.
unmutated.G2:required-dangling-refuses: The refusal half of G2, which has two ways to go wrong and both have entries: tolerating the dangling reference (DanglingTolerantGenerations, targeting G2:no-dangling, publishes the required rule that names nothing) and ignoring the refusal once it is made (FailOpenGenerations, targeting G1:refused-is-kept, publishes whatever survived). Both fail this label as well, because refused() is a required rule naming a missing structure, so it is the same law as those two labels and not a separate behaviour.
unmutated.G2:seeded-refusal: The seeded model of G2 (300 random offers against an independent oracle) restates G2:no-dangling, G2:optional-dropped-transitively and G1:refused-is-kept at volume: whether an offer is refused or published must match the oracle. DanglingTolerantGenerations (G2:no-dangling) and FailOpenGenerations (G1:refused-is-kept) both fail it, so the ground has covering entries; it is the sweep that guards against a hand-built scenario missing a combination, and has no mistake of its own.
unmutated.G2:seeded-survivors: The seeded model of G2 compared on the exact published set: restates G2:no-dangling and G2:optional-dropped-transitively on random offers, and both DanglingTolerantGenerations (G2:no-dangling) and ShallowDropGenerations (G2:optional-dropped-transitively) fail it. It is the sweep against hand-built scenarios, not a separate law; the exact survivor set is also what an implementation that drops too much (a policy mistake, see G2:broken-optional-left-out) would fail.
unmutated.G3:fixed-hashing: Asserted on every publication in the run: each manifest fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical content and the generation hash is Hashing.generation of the manifest. It is the continuous form of G3:golden and G3:order-independent: the five hashing entries (PartOrderHashGenerations, MapOrderHashGenerations, Utf16OrderHashGenerations, ContentBlindHashGenerations, InterpreterBlindHashGenerations) all fail it as well as their own targets, so every realistic way to compute another hash is already killed, and G3:golden pins the bytes. No mistake of its own.
unmutated.G4:consecutive: The exact form of G4:monotonic (ConstantNumberGenerations): the first publication is 1, each next is one more, and a refusal takes no number. ConstantNumberGenerations, PiecewiseGenerations (several publications per offer) and FailOpenGenerations (a refusal publishes and takes a number) all fail it, so the ground is covered. A counter that advances on a refusal or skips a number but only rises would pass G4:monotonic and is reached only by this label; no entry isolates it, so a mutant of that kind would be a fair addition.
unmutated.G5:immutable: A property of the shared model and not of an implementation: Generation is a record whose constructor copies the manifest and the diagnostics into unmodifiable collections, every Generations implementation can only make one through it, and the assembler's own value is built fresh for each candidate. The label checks that a held generation is unchanged by later offers and that its collections refuse writes; an implementation cannot defeat it without altering the Generation record, which the pure layer pins, so there is no implementation-level mutant to write.
unmutated.G6:named: Every finding has a non-empty code and message. The code half cannot be broken by an implementation: the Diagnostic constructor rejects an empty code, so no Generations implementation can emit one. The message half guards only the findings an implementation writes itself (offer:missing-kind, reference:dangling and the like); the assembler's own findings come from the harness. No matrix entry writes a blank message, a cheap mistake that would be caught here, so a mutant is possible but a minor one.
unmutated.G6:refusal-says-why: Every refusal in the run, whatever refused it, carries at least one finding. It restates G6:all-findings (FirstFindingGenerations): a report that drops findings fails both, and G6:all-findings names the exact codes on the richest refusal. What this adds is the refusals that scenario does not reach, such as the build refusal for a candidate with no rules; the shape refusals (G8:offer-shape) and the accounting refusals (G7:unlisted-refuses, G7:unoffered-refuses) also assert their own finding codes. Only NoOpGenerations, which refuses everything silently, fails it.
unmutated.G7:nothing-invented: The accounting law's second half, 'nothing is published that was not offered': every manifest entry must have an offered record. It is the same mistake as G7:accounted (TrustingGenerations takes the assembler's parts without checking the offer, so an invented entry is published), and TrustingGenerations fails this label too. The refusal side of the same accounting is G7:unoffered-refuses.
unmutated.G7:optional-rejection-left-out: The rejection form of the optional rule: a file the catalog rejected from an optional kind leaves the generation with whatever names it, and is named as catalog:rejected. It restates G2:optional-dropped-transitively (ShallowDropGenerations) and G2:broken-optional-left-out through the Snapshot.rejected() list; DanglingTolerantGenerations and FirstFindingGenerations fail it incidentally. An implementation that ignores Snapshot.rejected() entirely, or that makes OPTIONAL refuse, is not in the matrix and would be caught here (and by G7:required-rejection-refuses).
unmutated.G7:required-error-refuses: A required entry that an ERROR finding names refuses the candidate. It is the same refusal as G1:refused-is-kept (FailOpenGenerations), which fails it too, because FailOpenGenerations notes the refusal and publishes anyway. The mistake of its own, treating a required kind's ERROR finding as an optional drop, is not isolated by any entry; the policy half of the same law is G2:required-dangling-refuses.
unmutated.G7:required-rejection-refuses: A file the catalog rejected from the required kind refuses the candidate and is named. It is the same refusal as G1:refused-is-kept (FailOpenGenerations), which fails it as well. An implementation that never reads Snapshot.rejected() is not in the matrix and would be caught here and by G7:optional-rejection-left-out; otherwise it adds no behaviour that G1:refused-is-kept does not pin.
unmutated.G7:unlisted-refuses: The refusal half of G7:accounted: an entry the assembler gave neither a part nor a finding refuses the candidate with assembler:unlisted-entry. TrustingGenerations, which targets G7:accounted, fails it, as does FailOpenGenerations (which publishes the refused candidate). Same ground as G7:accounted; this label pins the finding code.
unmutated.G7:unoffered-refuses: The refusal half of G7:accounted for the opposite error: a part for an entry nobody offered refuses the candidate with assembler:unoffered-part. TrustingGenerations (G7:accounted) and FailOpenGenerations (G1:refused-is-kept) both fail it. Same ground as G7:accounted and G7:nothing-invented.
unmutated.G8:offer-shape: The malformed-offer half of G8: a missing kind or an undeclared one is refused with offer:missing-kind or offer:unknown-kind and the live generation serves on. G8:never-throws (EscapingGenerations) covers an exception escaping, and PiecewiseGenerations fails this label as well because it slices the offer. An implementation that quietly ignores an undeclared snapshot, or publishes a missing kind as empty, is not in the matrix and is reached only here; a mutant of that kind would be a fair addition.
unmutated.G8:threw-is-kept: The containment half of G8, 'what the assembler throws, in read or in build, ends as a refusal with assembler:threw': the escape is G8:never-throws (EscapingGenerations), which fails this label too (no outcome), and the live generation staying is G1:refused-keeps-current (DisturbingGenerations). What it adds, the specific code and the Kept outcome for each phase, has no mistake of its own beyond those two.
unmutated.P1:every-entry-published: A check on the consistent scenario with the exact manifest: the published manifest equals every offered entry of world A. The ways to publish less are closed elsewhere: an entry that vanishes unnamed is G7:accounted (TrustingGenerations), and a wrongly dropped one is the exact survivor set in G2:seeded-survivors (DanglingTolerantGenerations, ShallowDropGenerations). No mistake of its own that those do not pin; P1:consistent-published (NoOpGenerations) covers that a consistent candidate is published at all.
unmutated.P1:warnings-carried: A positive control on the reference's report: a WARNING on an entry that reads and publishes is carried on the generation's diagnostics (world A's odd t:r2). It guards the report, not the resolution, and no matrix entry filters warnings out of a published generation's findings; an implementation that keeps only the dropped-entry errors would pass every other label, because G2:dropped-reported and G7:accounted read only named subjects. A cheap mistake, so a mutant that publishes with only error findings would earn the label.
